entities.summary: Omar Tiberiades or Abū Ḥafṣ ʿUmar ibn al-Farrukhān al-Tabari was a prominent Medieval Persian astrologer and architect from the region of Tabaristan, known for his significant contributions to the field of astronomy. Born in unknown circumstances, he lived during the reign of the Abbasid Caliphate and is believed to have been influenced by the works of ancient Greek and Roman astronomers. His most notable work, the 'Book of the Calculation of Times', provided a comprehensive system for calculating the timing of celestial events and was widely used by scholars throughout the Islamic world. Omar Tiberiades' work had a lasting impact on the development of astronomy in the Middle Ages, influencing later scholars such as Ibn Yunus and Al-Biruni. His legacy extends beyond his scientific contributions, as he also played a key role in the construction of several important buildings in Tabaristan, including the Mosque of Saman. Omar Tiberiades' life and work provide a fascinating glimpse into the intellectual and cultural landscape of the Medieval Islamic world, highlighting the significant role that Persian scholars played in shaping the course of astronomy and architecture during this period. The Persian scholar's work continues to be studied and admired by scholars today, a testament to the enduring power of his scientific and architectural contributions.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Omar Tiberiades was a prominent Persian scholar who made significant contributions to the field of astronomy and architecture during the Medieval period. His work had a lasting impact on the development of astronomy in the Islamic world and influenced later scholars such as Al-Biruni.
